text:
The power failure points to the tail device M5. Its branch current is about 189 µA, nearly all of the 235 µA supply draw (189 + 35.6 µA output stage + 10 µA reference, at 1.8 V ≈ 423 µW). It is also in triode (Vds = 0.129 V < Vdsat = 0.242 V), so it is not acting as a current source. Its sizing (W = 2.02 µm, L = 0.15 µm, W/L ≈ 13.5) is far too large against the reference M6 (W/L ≈ 0.21). The reference and output mirror M8 look consistent with M6 at 10 µA, so M5 is the most likely corrupted element. M6 and M8 are next in the ranking because they set the bias node that drives M5's gate.

```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "M8"], "fault": "M5 (tail current source) is oversized/mis-sized (W=2.02 um, L=0.15 um, W/L about 64x the reference M6 ratio), so it sinks about 189 uA instead of roughly half that, pushing it into triode (Vds=0.129 V < Vdsat=0.242 V). This drives total supply current to about 235 uA (423 uW vs 180 uW limit). Fix: reduce M5 W/L (for example, W down to about 0.5-0.6 um at L=0.15 um, or lengthen L) so the tail current is roughly 50 uA and M5 returns to saturation."}
```
